description: How the generated binding of a raw relation stores its values in the projection (ontology/store_ddl.py layout v10, binding value_storage). packed: every currency-free value of one source record is one packed record (a JSON array under a shared layout) instead of one row per value, and those values are not word-indexed: plx.find reaches the records by object type and property filters, by their key and by their links; plx.object, plx.read, plx.around and every value reader read them as before. For wide, high-volume ledger and line relations whose cells are mostly codes, zeros and blank padding, where one row per value cost about 65 bytes and three B-tree inserts each. A relation not listed stores cells (word-indexed text). A listed relation that is not a generated binding of its source fails the generation, so a typo never silently changes nothing.
evidence: Measured on the live projection, generation 00000015 (2026-10-27, 248 Portal relations, 9.47 GB): 74,591,972 value cells took 4.9 GB (value_cells 1,988 MB, object_values_by_property 1,607 MB, its unique index 1,355 MB); the 14 Sage AP relations below held 70.3M of them (counts per relation in its entry: records, value cells). Text search over them (value_text) held 99 MB in all: the words are codes, zeros and padding.
